This motivates, but does not establish, complement coverage. Mechanism hypothesis: recent uninterrupted absence of a target field can encode interruption length in ordered timestamp groups (not elapsed time) that matching-prefix products suppress and that global absence mass cannot locate. Other IDs are heterogeneous, so absence is not evidence of a shared competing interest. No local complement measurement or predictive gain has yet been observed.

Unknown targets/fields/actions never create nonmatches; G<=1 zero. Fractional ties mean expectations under independent uniform draws per timestamp group, not an inferred within-tie ordering. falsifiers: No AUC advantage of nonmatch_run over nonmatch_mass weakens the contiguity account for this implementation, even if both beat matching cells.
A failure to improve the incumbent means the new mechanism is not selected; one unsuccessful fixed-scale implementation does not refute all possible absence-duration models.

alternative_explanations: Complement prefixes may mostly encode total known-field activity when no target match exists; in those coordinates C=M, so mass is the key replacement control.
Higher density/gradient exposure or reuse of already implicit self-recency may help optimization without a novel temporal mechanism. Fixed formal scale does not equalize empirical variances.
An apparent improvement may be seed noise, repeated-validation selection, an exposure-frequency proxy, snapshot leakage risk, or censoring at128 events.

DIN/DMR and all five external industry cards are reference evidence only; source-to-code provenance does not establish transfer or source-value causality.
